transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (CSM), Diego Suarez (SE) -- Tideway: Aisha Rahman (CTO), Liam O'Connor (Platform Lead), Priya Desai (Security Lead), Samir Kapoor (ML Engineer), Nora Flynn (PM), Ben Wu (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We've got Jordan on CSM and Diego on the technical side. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Aisha Rahman: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get started.
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Likewise. We have a pretty packed agenda; want to make sure we cover the sprint and security.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Yep, perfect. Quick runthrough of goals: align on success criteria for the onboarding, share the 3-week sprint plan, clarify security and network requirements for POC, and confirm data/throughput profiles so Diego can run perf/cost estimates.
[00:25] Priya Desai: From security we mainly need SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML details, encryption at rest and KMS options, and network diagrams for VPC peering or private deploy.
[00:32] Jordan Patel: We'll bundle the security pack. I can also include our standard support SLA and audit log retention options.
[00:36] Ben Wu: Procurement will want an SOW and pricing worksheet to review internally.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Totally. I'll send a draft SOW and the pricing worksheet after this call.
[00:44] Nora Flynn: For success criteria — we want to validate latency under typical user traffic, cost per 1M requests, and correctness compared to our baseline model outputs. Also an integration checklist so the product team can sign off.
[00:55] Diego Suarez: Great. On the technical side, a couple of clarifying questions: what model family are you planning to serve? Are you looking at a smaller, distilled model or a larger LLM for more nuanced responses? Also what's your typical sequence length distribution?
[01:06] Samir Kapoor: We're planning two tracks: inference for conversational triage (short sequences ~ 64-128 tokens) and document summarization (300-1024 tokens). Right now we're prototyping with open-weights models, likely variants of Llama 3-ish, but we may evaluate quantized mixes.
[01:20] Diego Suarez: Okay that helps. For initial cost estimates, I'll give you a delta between hosted Redwood API versus Dedicated (reserved GPU) and our Private deployment flavor (VPC/on-prem). Quantization and batching profiles will impact unit cost and latency.
[01:32] Liam O'Connor: On dedicated, what's the typical up-front commitment? We're trying to map that to our team budget cycles.
[01:36] Maya Chen: Dedicated is usually a monthly or annual reserved capacity contract. We can show examples — Diego has some bench numbers for 8xA100 and 4xA10 configurations.
[01:45] Diego Suarez: I can share a spreadsheet with throughput, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens for each config. Note that for shorter sequences continuous batching and prefix caching give big wins — that's our KV cache, sometimes transcribed in notes as "KV cash" but it's KV cache.
[01:58] Priya Desai: If we do private deployment inside our VPC, what's the control plane model? Are logs sent to Redwood or stored locally?
[02:05] Jordan Patel: For Redwood Private, the control plane is customer-managed and you can choose to keep logs inside your network; we also offer an option to ship redacted telemetry. We support KMS integrations for key management.
[02:16] Priya Desai: Great. Also need to know about RBAC and SSO support. We use Okta.
[02:21] Diego Suarez: We support SAML/Okta for SSO, RBAC roles at route/model levels. We'll include exact steps in the security packet.
[02:27] Aisha Rahman: For compliance, how do you handle data retention and audit logs? We're regulated and need read-only audit exports.
[02:33] Jordan Patel: We have configurable retention and audit exports. For Private deployments you can store logs internally; for hosted we retain logs per the agreed retention in the SLA. We'll include sample export formats.
[02:42] Nora Flynn: Sprint plan — what's the proposed cadence? Two-week sprints? We were hoping to go faster for the first POC to validate perf in a week.
[02:49] Maya Chen: We typically do a 3-week onboarding sprint: week 1: environment/setup & sample workload; week 2: run perf tests and iterate on batching/quant; week 3: integration + stabilization and handoff. But if you want a fast POC we can compress week 1-2 into a 7-10 day window for an initial perf report.
[03:05] Liam O'Connor: That sounds good. We prefer the fast loop for perf.
[03:08] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll mark a "fast-track POC" option. Diego, can you commit to running bench on their sample workloads if Samir provides the token distribution CSV?
[03:15] Diego Suarez: Yes — I'll run tests on hosted endpoints and a dedicated-equivalent config. If you can provide 1) sample request traces, 2) a few representative prompts, and 3) expected concurrency, that will let me get accurate numbers.
[03:25] Samir Kapoor: We can export traces from our staging harness. I'll get those over by Monday.
[03:29] Priya Desai: A question on encryption for model weights in Private deployment — is there support for encrypted model files with HSM?
[03:35] Diego Suarez: We support KMS integrations for key wrapping. For on-prem, customers can choose to use an HSM or a customer-managed KMS. I'll add notes in the security pack but it's supported.
[03:43] Ben Wu: About pricing — can we get a side-by-side estimate for expected monthly spend for the POC vs. projected production (100k users)? Procurement needs ranges.
[03:51] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll provide ranges: expected POC spend (hosted) and an extrapolation for production under hosted and dedicated scenarios. Diego will add quantized model estimates.
[03:59] Liam O'Connor: Any constraints on IP or data residency? We need EU data to stay in region for certain users.
[04:05] Jordan Patel: We have regional deployment options and can pin traffic to EU regions; for Private on-prem or VPC you control residency entirely.
[04:12] Aisha Rahman: How do we handle rollback or graceful degradation if a model update causes quality regression?
[04:17] Diego Suarez: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to a pinned model variant if a regression is detected. We also tie regressions to prompt-based evals.
[04:27] Nora Flynn: Fine. For the integration checklist, we need clear API keys, token scopes, and example SDK calls.
[04:33] Jordan Patel: We'll include code snippets for both REST and SDK, and example roles for keys.
[04:38] Maya Chen: Quick logistics: we'll send the onboarding sprint plan, security packet, and the pricing worksheet today. Can we set the architecture deep-dive for next Tuesday? Liam, is there availability?
[04:47] Liam O'Connor: Yes, Tuesday AM works for most of the infra team. I'll confirm exact attendees and drop times.
[04:51] Samir Kapoor: We also want a short session to review tokenization differences — sometimes our tokenizer diverges from the open model runner and that can affect perf and costs.
[04:58] Diego Suarez: Good call. We'll schedule a tokenizer and prompt engineering mini-session during the perf week.
[05:02] Aisha Rahman: Any blockers on our side other than providing sample traces and scheduling?
[05:06] Priya Desai: We need to run this by InfoSec; so the sooner we get the security pack, the sooner we can move to sign-off.
[05:12] Jordan Patel: I'll prioritize the security pack and include a short FAQ aimed at InfoSec.
[05:15] Nora Flynn: Ok, last thing — do you have a shared drive or workspace for docs? We prefer using a shared Confluence or Google Drive.
[05:21] Maya Chen: We'll create a shared Google Drive folder and drop the onboarding artifacts there. I'll send invites after the call.
[05:26] Ben Wu: After procurement reviews the SOW we'll need 2 weeks for legal redlines. Is that typical?
[05:30] Maya Chen: That's within normal time. For Dedicated we prefer earlier lock-in but we can align timelines.
[05:35] Diego Suarez: I'll also add a note about fallback model variants and automated SLO alerts in the console.
[05:39] Maya Chen: Great. To recap next steps: Jordan will send security pack; Diego will run perf estimates once samples are in; Maya will share SOW and sprint plan; Samir will send sample traces; Liam will confirm deep-dive attendees and times. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the architecture deep-dive.
[05:55] Aisha Rahman: Thanks everyone — looking forward to the POC.
[05:58] Maya Chen: Thanks all!

Notes about transcript quality: Some terms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cache" -> "KV cash", "Redwood" sometimes as "Red Wood"). This file retains speech-like artifacts, partial sentence fragments, and occasional overlaps.

References shared: https://redwood.ai/onboarding-sprint-template (deck), pricing_workbook_v2.xlsx (link), security_packet_redwood_2025.zip (link placeholder)
